programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc:
Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day.
In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Jason Manford hosts the fast-paced quiz show where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle down the Answer Run towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face the Final Run and earn the opportunity to take home their cash prize

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Quiz hosted by Susan Calman in which one contestant becomes the Boss and has to use judgement and tactics to decide which player is best suited to answer questions

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's railway journey through Cumbria and Dumfriesshire heads to the hills as he follows in the footsteps of the Lakeland poets. In Keswick, he retraces the walks of Samuel Taylor Coleridge, discovering how one of his legendary routes has been used as a form of therapy. Michael also visits the ruins of Lowther Castle, once a grand gothic estate, now reborn as a garden

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Siobhan, her partner Timmie and their two young children hope to bring new life in Butlerstown, Co Cork, by renovating the old post office to become their forever home

programme.title: Vintage Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Witley Court in Worcestershire, where they discover an early puppet theatre, a Worcester plate made as a royal gift and a drawing by Salford artist LS Lowry. They also value a rare piece of early Staffordshire slipware, similar to the famous 'Ozzie the Owl'. First broadcast in 2004

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and the team value antiques at the Discovery Museum in Newcastle. Experts Anita Manning and Nick Davies examine hundreds of collectibles brought along by members of the public, and Paul learns about the landscape gardener Capability Brown

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale and Philippa Dunne test their general knowledge skills in a variety of trivia-based games

programme.title: Strictly: It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor returns with some training room exclusives, with a look at how some of the celebrities are getting on with their next dances. Also, a panel of Strictly pros pop by to reveal some dance secrets

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Comedians Lloyd Griffith and Rhys James face off in a battle of antiques while on a road trip around Wales and south west England. They're joined by jewellery pro Hettie Jago and coin specialist Tim Medhurst. In Pontypool, Rhys makes an unusual find in the form of a picture frame-cum-radio and in Monmouth, Lloyd uncovers a sporting score board

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The Porthcawl crew's training night is disrupted when a call comes in about a surfer in trouble below the cliffs at Rest Bay. During the peak of a cyclone known as Storm Amy, Bridlington's lifeboat is tasked to a Dutch trawler that has lost power 13 miles off the Yorkshire coast. The Calshot crew search in thick fog for a motorboat with engine failure - somewhere in the shipping lanes of the Solent

programme.title: The Book That Changed My Life
programme.desc: Inspired by her passion to get people reading, Queen Camilla joins four remarkable people to share the stories of books that shaped them. Warm, emotional and full of hope, the programme shows how reading can lift people up, open minds and even change lives in a celebration of the power inside every book

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Iain Stirling introduces comedians Harriet Dyer and Maria Shehata to the London's Hammersmith Apollo stage, where they perform their stand-up routines

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Analysis of the day's events, with Victoria Derbyshire

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: The BBC's world affairs editor reflects on the week's major global news stories, talking to local experts from around the world to go behind the headlines

programme.title: Being Muslim After 9/11
programme.desc: Journalists and film-makers Mobeen Azhar and Masood Khan revisit their archives, reconnect with old interviewees and meet a wider range of people with important stories to tell, seeking to understand how things have changed for British Muslims in the 25 years since the September 11 attacks

programme.title: Finding Britain's Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc: Part one of two. David meets the historians who have built the Register of British Slave Traders, piecing together a comprehensive picture of more than 13,000 individuals who were investors in the slave trade, showing the links between modern British institutions and the trade in human beings. He begins by revealing how the monarchy drove the early British slave trade, with Elizabeth I and the early Stuarts giving their support to early slavery ventures

programme.title: Rise of the Footsoldier 4: Marbella
programme.desc: Fresh out of prison, a former nightclub owner heads to Marbella to seek revenge against the man who put him away - but things quickly unravel. Action comedy, starring Craig Fairbrass, Emily Wyatt and Terry Stone

programme.title: Southern Fury
programme.desc: When his brother falls foul of a ruthless mobster, a straight-laced man calls on his old friend and cop to help out. Crime thriller, starring Adrian Grenier, John Cusack and Nicolas Cage

programme.title: Momentum
programme.desc: Action thriller starring Olga Kurylenko and James Purefoy. A glamorous jewel thief goes on the run from a master assassin when her face is accidentally revealed in the middle of a heist.

programme.title: Teleshopping

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures once more on to the European rail network to retrace journeys featured in George Bradshaw's 1913 publication Continental Guide, beginning by travelling through Russia. He starts in the industrial city of Tula, before visiting Leo Tolstoy's former home of Yasnaya Polyana and learning how the author's life and works were intertwined with the railways. Michael then boards the train that runs from the Caspian Sea to Moscow, where he performs an important role in a dramatic opera at the Bolshoi Theatre, before exploring the beauty and history of St Petersburg and riding on the first railway ever built in Russia

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo uses his 1913 copy of Bradshaw's Continental Railway Guide to explore Poland. He begins in the capital Warsaw, where he takes to the floor to dance to one of Chopin's polonaises with high-school students rehearsing for their leavers' ball, before discovering how the former industrial city of Lodz supplied the vast Russian empire of the early 20th century. He then heads to Poznan and rides one of the few remaining steam-powered commuter trains, visits a factory in Wroclaw that manufactures car bodies for locomotives, and ends his journey in Krakow, where he takes a tour in an iconic vehicle of the communist era

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman

programme.title: James Martin: Delicious

programme.title: James Martin: Delicious

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off

Hosted by Noel Fielding and Matt Lucas, with Prue Leith and Paul Hollywood deciding who will be leaving this week

programme.title: Classic Mary Berry
programme.desc: The food writer demonstrates a selection of her favourite recipes that have moved in and out of fashion, including her take on a classic prawn cocktail, as well as a rich onion soup, and a banoffee pie. programme.title: Paul Hollywood: City Bakes

programme.title: Jamie: Fast and Simple

programme.title: How the Tudors Lost Their Heads
programme.desc: Margaret Pole was born into England's ruling dynasty but lost her wealth and status when the Tudors came to power. Resilient and smart, she fought her way back to become one of the country's most powerful people. She was trusted by Henry VIII to be his daughter Mary's governess but was also willing to defy the king. Suzannah Lipscomb and Dan Snow trace Margaret's incredible story and investigate her downfall, exploring castles across England and heading to Europe on the trail of her son, Reginald. A protégé of Henry VIII, he turned against the king over the break with Catholic Rome. Reginald's 'betrayal' led to an international manhunt that endangered his family and eventually led to Margaret's conviction as a traitor. Killed at the age of 67, her execution is remembered as one of the most shocking of Tudor times.

programme.desc:
Today, Andrew Denly and wife Sheila from Sussex are hoping clockmaker Steve Fletcher can fix a vintage boy's toy with big memories attached. It's an antique toy cannon handed down to Andrew by his grandfather, who bought it with his pocket money in 1907. Andrew fondly describes his grandfather as his inspiration and boyhood hero. The little cannon is much treasured but hasn't worked in over 50 years. Steve must use all his ingenuity to get it firing once more.
A Victorian oddity is brought to the attention of leather expert Susie Fletcher. Sisters Pam and Frances are hoping Suzie can revive a novelty inkwell in the shape of a hat. It is a treasured family heirloom as it had huge sentimental value to the sisters' mother. After years of vigorous overuse, the button mechanism no longer works and it is missing its leather covering. Suzie drafts in sibling Steve Fletcher to help make a missing part, and she discovers a new talent for miniature millinery as she returns the inkwell to its stylish former glory.
Finally, ceramics expert Kirstin Ramsey prays for divine intervention as she tries to rebuild a saintly statue. Caroline Morson and Professor John Northover have come to the barn seeking help resurrecting an important icon that's been a symbol of hope to many: a statue of St Fiacre, the patron saint of gardeners and haemorrhoid victims! The statue has been a landmark in the garden of St Mark's Hospital, a centre for the treatment of bowel disease, for many years, but has been vandalised and is now broken in two. Gifted to the hospital by Caroline's father, renowned pathologist Dr Basil Morson, staff and patients alike are keen to see St Fiacre restored and back on duty. By far one of the biggest projects Kirsten has had on her bench, she must clean and reunite the two large broken halves, creating an imperceptible join to breathe new life into this old saint.

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The third stay is at the Quay Inn in Minehead, Somerset, where Collette Whiteoak and Danny Kelly are confident their traditional pub atmosphere will be a hit with their rivals. But there are a few cleanliness issues, and the battle of the banger continues over breakfast

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: Justin Head and Mike Smyth host the final visit of the week at Old Walls Vineyard Luxury Lodges in Bishopsteignton in Devon. Come feedback time, Justin and Mike are left feeling furious

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The B&Bers meet for the last time to find out how much they've been paid and to settle some scores. programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Alarm-company owner Bill Black kicks off a series of dinner parties in Dundee, where he hopes his belt-busting menu will impress his guests - proud Arbroathian Phil Petrie, English student Hannah Wilson, ferret fancier Alex Pithouse and 28-year-old Kim Gillespie - and make him an early contender for the £1,000 prize

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Architectural technician Alex Pithouse hosts the second dinner party in Dundee, and aims to impress his guests by giving them an education in fine dining, complete with a complex menu and some good wines, as well as by introducing them to his three pet ferrets

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Vegetarian Hannah Wilson prepares an Italian feast for her guests in Dundee, and in a bid to win over her carnivore guests she devises a cunning plan that involves dishing up some meat with the starter

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: The fourth night in Dundee is hosted by self-styled food critic Phil Petrie, who has been unimpressed with the culinary standard so far. He hopes to impress with his evening, but things begin to go wrong when he runs out of ingredients and leaves his guests feeling hungry

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: On the final night in Dundee, Kim Gillespie plans an ambitious menu, largely based on Yorkshire delights, with exotic dishes from Spain and Thailand also featuring - all accompanied by a Scottish choir singing American songs

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The first visit of the week is to Newton House in Knaresborough, North Yorkshire, where Denise Carter and Jackie Fennell's traditional B&B focuses on organic, free-range breakfasts. Over dinner, guest Marianne Cammack and Deina Thomas from dominate the conversation, riling up some of the others, while Mike Hayes and Neal Widdowson think the morning meal is all way too fancy

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The second visit of the competition is to the Highlands Pub in Blackpool, where managers Mike Hayes and Neal Widdowson are all about value for money. However, Sean and Kathryn are horrified by what they find in their room, while Marianne and Deina think that theirs needs the female touch. In the afternoon the group competes in a basketball challenge at the amusement arcades, where the quiet hosts come out of their shells

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The contestants travel to the White House in Brighton for the third day of the competition, where hosts Sean Edlin and Kathryn Turnbull run a laid-back seaside B&B. Denise and Jackie think the rooms are not well equipped and Marianne finds them clinical, while Mike and Neal are unsure about the price. Tensions are temporarily alleviated by a visit to the famous Theatre Royal, but Marianne and Deina continue to cause trouble at dinner. In the morning, a locally sourced breakfast impresses some of the guests, but the group must decide whether they are getting value for money

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: Wakes Hall Lodges near Colchester is the fourth and final visit of the week, where Neal and Mike are wowed by the five-star self-catering accommodation, complete with hot tubs and lakeside views. The others aren't so sure about the 'luxury' breakfast hamper, however, especially as it means cooking their own. An afternoon of dog agility gives manager Marianne Cammack the chance to demonstrate her authority, although over dinner, her domineering conversation causes Jackie to finally snap

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The B&B owners meet for the last time to find out what they've been paid and to settle some scores. programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Experts Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott head to the seaside in Lincolnshire, for their last chance to hit the shops before the final auction showdown. At the shops, Irita comes over all nostalgic as she stumbles across items from her childhood. She also gets her hands on some exquisite, enamelled artwork that she feels would benefit from being dismantled. Raj racks up a haul of potential purchases, but still finds time for a spot of puppetry. He also discovers the birthplace of the package holiday and meets the town's jovial mascot who has been pulling in the punters for over 100 years

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Jay Blades and the team bring three treasured family heirlooms, and the memories they hold, back to life.
First to arrive is Eleanor Grundell from Leeds. She has her hopes pinned on master goldsmith Richard Talman saving two rings with huge meaning. The engagement and eternity rings were the beautiful possessions of her grandma Edna, whom Eleanor sadly never met but heard so much about from her late father. Eleanor views these rings as a vital link to those beloved family members and intends to wear them, should she get married one day. However, the rings in their current condition are too fragile to wear, with missing precious stones and misshapen beyond belief.
The barn's next visitors are Richard and Kath Bond, along with Dobbin the geriatric pantomime horse, much to the glee of soft toy restorers Amanda Middleditch and Julie Tatchell. Richard, Kath and Dobbin are all members of their local amateur dramatic club and have been since the 1960s. Dobbin even made a cameo appearance at their wedding ceremony. Although Kath has tried unsuccessfully to repair his various issues, he is falling apart and in no fit state to tread the boards.
And stringed instrument expert Julyan Wallis takes on a much-loved dreadnought guitar in a diabolical condition. Owner Walter Renton played professionally in various bands in his heyday and wooed his wife with love songs played on this very instrument. His daughter Ann is immensely proud of him and not just for his musical talent. Recently Walter has been very poorly but is now well on the road to recovery. Being able to play his old guitar, that he bought over 50 years ago, would give him and his loving family hope for the future.

programme.desc: Food writer Mary Berry is one of Britain's best-loved TV cooks, finding fame thanks to her judging role on The Great British Bake Off. A self-confessed go-getter, she wants to trace her family tree to know where she gets her energy and drive from. The journey begins in Bath, where Mary grew up, and takes her to Norwich, where both her grandparents lived. Her body would later be found in the undergrowth by a massive search operation, having died of hypothermia. The first episode examines the early clues that were discovered and the suspicion that fell on a childhood friend and his grandmother, before they were released without charge

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures once more on to the European rail network to retrace journeys featured in George Bradshaw's 1913 publication Continental Guide, beginning by travelling through Russia. He starts in the industrial city of Tula, before visiting Leo Tolstoy's former home of Yasnaya Polyana and learning how the author's life and works were intertwined with the railways. Michael then boards the train that runs from the Caspian Sea to Moscow, where he performs an important role in a dramatic opera at the Bolshoi Theatre, before exploring the beauty and history of St Petersburg and riding on the first railway ever built in Russia

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Steered by his 1913 Bradshaw railway guide, Michael Portillo takes the train down the spine of Italy as he travels from Rome to Sicily. He begins by weaving among the capital city's landmarks on the back of a 1950s Vespa, before boarding the train south to Naples, where he finds out about the first railway to be built in the country, and ventures into the crater of Mount Vesuvius. He takes a detour to the island of Capri, before finishing his journey in the ancient hilltop town of Taormina

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo uses his 1913 copy of Bradshaw's Continental Railway Guide to explore Poland. He begins in the capital Warsaw, where he takes to the floor to dance to one of Chopin's polonaises with high-school students rehearsing for their leavers' ball, before discovering how the former industrial city of Lodz supplied the vast Russian empire of the early 20th century. He then heads to Poznan and rides one of the few remaining steam-powered commuter trains, visits a factory in Wroclaw that manufactures car bodies for locomotives, and ends his journey in Krakow, where he takes a tour in an iconic vehicle of the communist era

programme.title: Finding Britain's Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc: Part one of two. David meets the historians who have built the Register of British Slave Traders, piecing together a comprehensive picture of more than 13,000 individuals who were investors in the slave trade, showing the links between modern British institutions and the trade in human beings. programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc:
Danny is joined by Sybil, the manager of a charity shop in the home counties. From the day she opened, Sybil felt a strange presence, which only heightened when other workers also said they sensed someone in the shop with them.
As time went on and more workers had the same experience, activity began to ramp up. Things started to move in front of multiple witnesses, and when building work was done on the shop, the presence finally revealed itself - to terrifying effect.
After the discovery of a hidden room, clues as to who this presence could be come to light. Danny does some digging into the building's past and finds some extraordinary leads as to who could be responsible, while also exploring the phenomenon of stone tape theory, where past events are somehow recorded in the fabric of buildings.
As ever, the audience is invited to share their theories and help crack the case.

programme.desc:
A once-beautiful mid-century coffee table has been part of owner Graham's life for 60 years. The much-loved item belonged to his parents and took pride of place in their living room. It is the first toy owner Gill remembers having and was a gift from her late father, who tragically died two weeks before her sixth birthday aged just 52. After providing 50 years of comfort and support to Gill, panda is looking worse for wear, and it's a tearful moment as they are reunited.
An unusual and ingenious contraption arrives for the attention of metal worker Dominic Chinea. It is a coconut scraper and was the creation of Dudley's father, who migrated with his family to the UK from India in 1958. Dudley and his brothers have fond memories of helping their mother make a Goan treat called Kulkuls. It's down to Dom to get the rusted utensil back into service so the brothers can preserve this childhood memento and recreate the famous and much-loved sweet treats.

programme.desc:
Jay Blades and the team bring three treasured family heirlooms, and the memories they hold, back to life.
Mother and son duo Linda and James Gibson are in desperate need of silversmith Brenton West's help to restore a treasured lead statue of a young man with a dog that has been part of their family for over 70 years. Originally bought by Linda's parents, the statue stood proudly in their garden all through Linda's childhood. The statue was stolen and thought lost forever until several years later it was discovered in a ditch and returned to the delighted family. The dashing young man and his faithful hound incurred extensive damage in the incident and are looking very sorry for themselves. This is one of the largest projects Brenton has ever undertaken, and he is determined to get the figure back on his feet again.
Next at the barn to meet expert Suzie Fletcher is Dawn Curley from the West Midlands. She has brought her late father's suitcase, which is made from cardboard. This trusty little case carried all of Leopard's possessions on the Empire Windrush voyage from Jamaica in 1948. Leopard settled in the UK, fell in love and had a large family. His daughter Dawn is very proud of what her father achieved despite much prejudice and discrimination and feels compelled to have this crumpled case preserved in his memory.
And French polisher Will Kirk repairs a wooden giraffe that belonged to Illona's late husband Steve, who loved the lofty creatures. She bought it as a gift for him. Tragically, Steve passed away not long after they were married and this giraffe, who she has named Steve, reminds her of the happy times they had together. However, the wood has split and damaged, which rendered the poor thing lame and unstable.

programme.title: Loch Lomond: A Year in the Wild
programme.desc: The winter is mild and wet, which is good news for some but bad news for others at Loch Lomond and Trossachs National Park. Cameras follow red deer who are forced to move up to higher ground, while salmon have survived six months without food. Meanwhile, mountain hares turn an inconspicuous white to help them hide from predators, but with no snow they have become easy targets for hungry eagles

programme.title: Digging Up Britain's Past
programme.desc: Centuries ago, canals were the liquid highways of Britain, transporting raw materials and finished goods all over the country. Their arrival kick-started the Industrial Revolution, which was to turn Britain into a superpower. The very first water superhighway was the Bridgewater Canal, completed in 1761 to carry coal to Manchester from the mines in Worsley. Here, a team of archaeologists from Salford University roots out this industrial past, working with volunteers to excavate the very coal mine that inspired the creation of the canal

programme.title: Ben Fogle: New Lives in the Wild
programme.desc: Ben journeys to the African continent to meet Aleks, a Norwegian model who now resides in the deserts of Botswana. Aleks introduces him to her adopted family - the Ju'/hoansi people who have called southern Africa home for hundreds of thousands of years. Ben helps assemble bush fences to protect against desert lions and learns how the Scandinavian model ended up in Africa. The show also features Ralph Bousfield, owner of Uncharted Africa and part of Natural Selection

programme.title: Ben Fogle: New Lives in the Wild
programme.desc: Ben meets fellow Brit Rupert, who resides in the mountains of Japan in a traditional house. As Ben delves into Rupert's story, he uncovers the reasons behind his move to Japan and sees how content his host has become

programme.title: James May's Great Explorers
programme.desc: Captain James Cook was the last explorer in the age of sail - and one of the busiest, charting one third of the globe. His voyages brought huge advancements in navigation, biology, and geography, and in Britain he is generally thought of as a hero - but in other parts of the world, that's not the story. James May examines how this studious and serious son of a farmer broke through the class ceiling to become the greatest naval captain of his age

programme.desc: A critically endangered antelope is losing weight fast and needs urgent surgery, a baby rhino takes her first steps out on the savannah to meet her extended family for the very first time, a dig-happy warthog gets the perfect piggy pedicure, and a beloved manatee struggles with a toothache - time to visit the dentist!

programme.title: Heartland Docs
programme.desc: Erin performs life-saving surgery on a dog with a uterus ten times its normal size, while Ben tries to get to the bottom of what's ailing an underweight cow

programme.title: Wild Bhutan: The Last Shangri-La
programme.desc: Exploring a place between Tibet and India where nature and religion have combined to turn a tiny Buddhist kingdom into the world's last Shangri-La

programme.title: Wild Florida
programme.desc: Part one of two. Exploring the wildlife of the US state's coral islands, mangroves and sandy beaches - including crocodiles, sharks, rattlesnakes and birds of prey

programme.title: Investigation Shark Attack
programme.desc: Encounters with great white sharks are rising in California, and the team investigates why. Shark conservation has led to a population boom, and with warming waters, adaptable sharks keep moving further north. Drone footage provides a fascinating new window into shark behavior and proves just how often sharks are in close proximity to humans-without incident.

programme.title: Britain's Greatest Machines with Chris Barrie
programme.desc: The actor and engineering enthusiast revisits the battles of the Falklands War as he seeks out the greatest machines of the 1980s and takes a ride in a DeLorean DMC-12, as seen in Back to the Future

programme.title: Yukon Vet
programme.desc: Dr Oakley prepares animals for the harsh winter ahead, treating a llama with an inflamed eye and horses with dental damage and mysterious nosebleeds, before wrangling 85 cows

programme.title: Secrets of the Zoo: North Carolina
programme.desc: Keepers hope for a long-awaited sand cat kitten; a nervous puffin chick learns to swim, and rescued black bear cubs prepare for life outside the zoo

programme.title: Fish My City
programme.desc: Mike Iaconelli visits Miami to catch six different species of fish, including three exotic varieties that have travelled a long way to the city's freshwater canals

programme.title: Fish My City
programme.desc: Mike Iaconelli travels to New Orleans, where he braves challenging weather conditions and issues with the city's flood control system to catch a 10-foot long prehistoric predator

programme.title: Disaster Autopsy
programme.desc: Recreations of real-life disasters, using analysis and 3D graphics to uncover the factors behind the tragedies

programme.title: Ice Road Rescue
programme.desc: A 50-ton truck and trailer carrying asphalt has crashed above a steep bank. Boss Thord must save it before the ground gives way and causes a mudslide.

programme.title: Savage Kingdom
programme.desc: Led by a ruthless commander, the rotten clan of hyenas seizes power from the lions. An exiled queen is hell bent on winning back the throne for the Matahta Pride. Pula, ruler of the dark heart of the kingdom, is forced to make a terrible choice between true love and her own future. And a wandering vagrant is lured in by the promise of paradise, only to find herself trapped in a deadly hell.

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow of Atomic Bombs
programme.desc: Part two of two. The hydrogen bomb age from Bikini to Kazakhstan, the closure of the Soviet Polygon and the broken promises of the Budapest Memorandum. Today, Russia uses nuclear threats to redraw borders and China builds its arsenal unchecked

programme.title: Weathered: Earth's Extremes
programme.desc: Maiya May journeys across the United States to explore climate tipping points. Discovering how critical climate systems are for the planet’s stability, and learning the science behind these changes

programme.title: Teleshopping
programme.desc: A chance for viewers to purchase goods from the comfort of home

programme.title: Teleshopping
programme.desc: A chance for viewers to purchase goods from the comfort of home

programme.title: Weathered: Earth's Extremes
programme.desc: Maiya May visits the Isle de Jean Charles, Louisiana, one of the first communities in the United States to undergo a federally funded relocation due to climate change. She also learns about hurricanes from the Hurricane Hunters

programme.title: Besieged Fortresses, Legendary Battles
programme.desc: Known as 'the Verdun of the 16th century', the siege of Malta opposes the huge Muslim Ottoman army to the Christian stronghold controlled by only 1700 men

programme.title: Edwardian Britain in Colour
programme.desc: Conclusion of the two-part documentary in which social historians examine surviving footage of Britain in the early years of the 20th century. This edition featuring clips of people celebrating the arrival of a new tram in Wigan, a football match in Burnley, and a public swimming gala in Tynemouth, and film of suffragette Emily Wilding Davison colliding with the king's horse at the 1913 Epsom Derby

programme.title: The Rosenbergs: Atomic Spies
programme.desc: How, in 1950 with America in the throes of the Red Scare, seemingly ordinary couple Julius and Ethel Rosenberg found themselves the target of anti-Communist hysteria. Arrested by the FBI and accused of passing secret information to the USSR, they maintained their innocence while the media and public opinion seemed to condemned them. Their trial did nothing to change this and ended in a death sentence. Thirty years later, declassified files revealed that Ethel was not a spy, though Julius did commit espionage - primarily as a recruiter. Using archival footage, this documentary revisits the intriguing case

programme.title: The Roman Fleet
programme.desc: The naval forces of Ancient Rome played a crucial role in the conquest of the Mediterranean and beyond - but how did the Roman fleet operate? To find answers, experimental archaeologists from the University of Trier reconstructed a full-scale historical replica of a Roman ship, using ancient craftsmanship and based on excavation findings.
